**`pm:retriage` — classification produced by the wrong seat, not a dispute about the content.**

This card was filed by a dev working under the `domain:ui` execution seat (session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`), on my instruction to sever an accept-set narrowing out of PR #6472. My instruction said explicitly: *"file the narrowing as its own card carrying your full measurement (unassigned, no grading labels — triage grades it)"*. The card arrived carrying `needs-user-decision`, `domain:ui` and **type `Feature`** — three classifications that belong to the triage seat alone.

⛔ I have not removed them, because stripping is a producer action too, and one of them may well be right. `pm:retriage` is attached alongside so triage confirms or corrects. Flagging it rather than quietly leaving it, because a card sitting in the maintainer's decision box with a `type` the executing lane invented is exactly the failure the single-producer rule exists to prevent.

Two specifics worth triage's attention:

- **`needs-user-decision` matches my ruling's intent.** I severed this precisely because it needs a maintainer, so if that label survives re-triage, nothing is lost.
- **`type: Feature` is the one I would look at hardest.** The mechanical boundary test keys on *widening* the accepted set or the public surface. This change **narrows** it — parsing a previously-unvalidated `gantt` block against the spec's schema makes the CLI's `validate`/`check` refuse documents they used to accept. "Shrinks the accept set" is not the same as "widens it", so `Feature` may be the wrong side of a test that does not cleanly cover this direction. That is triage's call, not mine.

The measurement on this card is sound and I am not asking for it to be re-derived — the dev's zero-casualty scan (5095 tracked files) and the observation that the renderer already validates this block and warns are both accurate. My reason for severing was never that the change is wrong; it was that a published tool's refusal behaviour should not ride along inside a PR titled for declaring 28 keys.

PR #6472 has been verified severed on head `2760b32a6` — no bare `gantt` member in `ObjectGanttSchema`, no `gantt` key in the zod mirror, and the 25 derived members plus all nine moved members intact — and is now armed to land.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — Option A: declare the `gantt` block face; the spec's required trio enforces immediately, no warning window

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-27, PM chat decision-inbox batch 7 (adjudication session `session_01DKWDdUJ2XNRESVVWUvcpnh`), verbatim: 「以上同意」 — accepting recommendation A. The fallback C (a one-release warning window) is excluded by the maintainer's standing startup-stage no-gradualism rule (2026-08-27, objectstack-ai/objectstack#12668): transitions do not get phased windows without named external-user evidence, and none exists here. ⛔ B (relaxing the spec's requiredness on the objectui face) stays declined — no vocabulary fork.

Ruled: declare `gantt` on both faces (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` + the zod mirror via the existing `GanttConfigExtensionFields`), so the spec's required trio (`startDateField`, `endDateField`, `titleField`) is enforced at validate/check time. A block missing the trio moves from "accepted, silently broken at runtime" to "refused loudly at authoring time" — surfacing existing breakage, not creating new (in-repo census: 5095 files, zero casualty blocks; an out-of-repo block missing the trio is already non-functional at runtime today).

Dispatch notes: re-take the measurement on `main` after PR #6472's landing (the severance source); Clause-②: yes — this changes the published CLI's accept/reject behaviour, ruled here, contract-review tier; pins: trio-missing block refused (red-before-fix), trio-complete block accepted, plus the #6472 derived-pin family untouched.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

⛔ **C is excluded, and by a standing rule rather than by preference** — the maintainer's startup-stage no-gradualism rule (2026-08-27, objectstack-ai/objectstack#12668): transitions do not get phased windows without **named external-user evidence**, and none exists here. So ⛔ no warning window, no flag, no deprecation period. ⛔ B (relaxing the spec's requiredness on the objectui face) stays declined — no vocabulary fork.

## The framing that matters, because it is easy to state backwards

This **surfaces existing breakage; it does not create new breakage.** A `gantt` block missing the trio is *already* non-functional at runtime today — `getGanttConfig`'s block branch already feeds it to `GanttConfigSchema.safeParse` and logs `[ObjectGantt] Invalid gantt configuration`. What changes is **when the author is told**: runtime silence becomes an authoring-time refusal naming the field.

⭐ So this is a `declared = enforced` restoration, not a widening of the rules. The spec has required all three since rc.6; nothing here invents requiredness.

## ⚠️ Re-take the measurement — the ruling says so explicitly

The zero-casualty census (5095 tracked files, no metadata block missing the trio) was taken **before PR #6472 landed**, and this card was severed *out of* that PR. Re-run it on current `main`.

⚠️ And know the census's own trap, which the card records: the apparent `gantt` hits are **i18n translation namespaces** that happen to be named `gantt` (`packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`), prose, and `as any` test fixtures that never reach the zod mirror. ⛔ A bare grep for `gantt:` conflates those with authored metadata blocks. Report the populations separately.

## Clause-② — yes, ruled here

This changes a **published CLI's accept/reject behaviour** (`packages/cli/src/commands/{validate,check}.ts` reach it through `AnyComponentSchema` → `safeValidateSchema`). Contract-review tier at review. State in the PR body exactly what the CLI refuses after this that it accepted before.

⚠️ ⭐ Note for the record, because the classification was itself contested and resolved: this card is typed **`Feature`** even though the change *narrows* the accept set. Triage maintained it deliberately — the mechanical boundary test does not cleanly cover a narrowing, so the tie was broken on what the `type` field's readers do with it: `Bug`/`Task` are auto-adjudication candidates, `Feature` is mechanically barred to the manual floor. **A change to a published tool's refusal behaviour must not be auto-adjudicable by any future seat.** ⛔ Do not "correct" the type.

## Pins the ruling names

- a trio-missing block is **refused** — red before the fix;
- a trio-complete block is **accepted**;
- ⛔ #6472's derived-pin family stays **untouched** (`Exclude` of block-face keys against declared keys must remain `never`). That pin proves every block-face key is declared at the top level; it cannot prove the block key itself is — which is exactly the hole this card closes.

## Fence

`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`. `GanttConfigExtensionFields` already exists in the mirror (PR #6472 added it), so this is two lines plus pins.

⚠️ **`packages/types` is shared right now.** #6527's B patch round holds `packages/types/src/index.ts` and that package's `exports` map in `package.json`. Different files from yours — but **report it** if your work reaches either, and ⛔ do not touch the `exports` map.

## What earns the accept

**The ruling was executed literally, and the two rejected options are recorded with their reasons** — Option A (declare as-is, spec requiredness enforces immediately), with C excluded by the standing no-gradualism rule and B declined because it forks the vocabulary from the spec. A PR that names what it did *not* do, and why, is reviewable a year from now.

**Clause ② is answered as a table, not a claim.** Exactly one cell moves: a `gantt` block present but missing any of the required trio goes from **accepted** (riding through `.passthrough()` unvalidated) to **refused, naming the missing field**. Trio-complete blocks and the flat/absent spellings are unchanged. That is the right shape for a narrowing — the accept set moves in one place and the PR says which.

**The framing is correct and matters:** this surfaces existing breakage rather than creating it. `getGanttConfig`'s block branch already fed the block to `GanttConfigSchema.safeParse` and already logged `[ObjectGantt] Invalid gantt configuration`. What changes is *when the author is told* — runtime console silence becomes an authoring-time refusal. `declared = enforced` restored; nothing here invents requiredness.

**The ablation is a real measurement.** Prediction stated before running; mutation confirmed **on disk by anchored counts, not by an editor's exit code** (`gantt?: GanttConfig;` 1→0, the zod line 1→0, the old severed-state marker 0→1); observed result matched exactly — `1 failed | 16 passed`, and the one failure is the predicted `toContain('gantt')` assertion. Restore proven by empty `git diff HEAD` plus `git hash-object` equality on both files, with the whole pin suite green again at 26/26.

**The census was re-taken on the current tree, not inherited.** The original scan predated #6472 and covered 5095 files; the tree is now 5641. ⭐ And it was taken the right way: a bare `grep "gantt:"` returns 121 hits across 56 files and **conflates unrelated populations**, so the dev separated eight of them — i18n namespaces literally named `gantt`, prose, view-type discriminator maps, `as any` fixtures that never reach the mirror, `ListViewSchema.gantt` (a *different* schema that already required the trio), doc fences, real authored JSON, and substring false-positives — with a positive control on the zeros. Net: zero trio-missing blocks in every population that can reach `ObjectGanttSchema`'s parser, **including** `examples/schema-catalog`'s 3 real authored JSON files, which are the closest thing in this repo to what a human or an agent would actually write.

⭐ The dev also recorded that those catalog files are **not machine-validated by any workflow today** (grepped `.github/workflows/**` for `schema-catalog`; only comments) — so this PR does not newly break CI on them, and the finding is that they would pass even if it did. That is the honest way to report a green: say what the green does and does not cover.

**The out-of-tree question stays recorded, not answered.** Whether authored `gantt` metadata missing `titleField` exists outside this repository is unmeasurable by an in-repo census by construction. The ruling chose A anyway under the no-gradualism rule. Correct to leave it stated rather than quietly implied to be zero.

**The fence held.** Only `objectql.ts`, its zod mirror, the one obsoleted pin, and the changeset. `packages/types/src/index.ts` and the `exports` map — held by #6527's B round — were not touched.

## ⭐⭐⭐ The finding inside this PR is worth more than the PR

The dev's own docstring broke an unrelated gate, and the mechanism generalizes:

> `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` re-check scans **raw text** between `export const` boundaries for a `\bSpec[A-Z]\w*` token. A docstring above the private `GanttConfigExtensionFields` const — textually between the `ObjectTreeSchema` and `ObjectGanttSchema` boundaries — mentioned `SpecGanttConfigSchema` **in prose**, and that mention was attributed to `ObjectTreeSchema`, which references no spec schema at all.

⇒ **A comment changed a gate's verdict.** The gate is a text scanner, not an AST reader, so prose inside the wrong pair of export boundaries is indistinguishable from a real reference — and the false attribution lands on the *neighbouring* export, not the one you edited. The dev fixed it by rewording and left a trap-marker comment for the next editor, which is the right call inside this fence.

But the gate still has the defect, and the next person to write a docstring in that file will meet it again with no warning. Filed as a separate card so it is fixed where it lives rather than worked around a second time.

Refs: #6472 (the `GanttConfigExtensionFields` map this reuses unchanged) · #6051 (the 28-key census this closes) · #6508 (a different pre-existing defect in the same `page-builder.md` example, correctly not restated here).

## What makes this report worth reading past the diff

**The census was re-taken, not re-cited.** The card's original scan predated #6472 and covered 5095 files; the tree is now 5641. A bare `grep -n "gantt:"` returns 121 hits across 56 files and conflates unrelated populations — exactly the trap the card itself warned about. The dev separated eight populations and put a positive control on the zeros:

- i18n namespaces literally named `gantt` (10 locale files) — never reach `ObjectGanttSchema`
- prose in CHANGELOGs and changeset bodies
- view-type discriminator/lookup maps keyed by the literal string
- `as any` test fixtures that never reach the zod mirror — **positive control**: `plugin-gantt` type-check clean, proving these are genuinely never parsed rather than silently `any`-typed
- `ListViewSchema.gantt` — a *different* schema that already took the spec's `GanttConfigSchema` unmodified, so it already required the trio and is untouched here
- doc/prose fences (all trio-complete)
- ⭐ **real authored JSON metadata** — `examples/schema-catalog` — 3 files, all trio-complete
- substring false positives (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `TimelineSchema`'s own `variant: 'gantt'`, a keywords entry)

Net: zero blocks missing the trio in every population that can plausibly reach the parser, **including the one population that is genuine authored metadata rather than a test fixture**. The dev also recorded that `examples/schema-catalog` is not machine-validated by any workflow today — confirmed by grepping `.github/workflows/**` — so the finding is that those files *would* pass, not that CI enforces them. That distinction is the difference between a measurement and a reassurance.

**The clause-② table is stated as a behaviour delta, not as prose.** Exactly one row moves: a `gantt` block missing any of the trio goes from accepted (riding through `.passthrough()` unvalidated) to refused, naming the missing field. Trio-complete blocks and the flat spelling are unchanged. And the framing is right: a block missing the trio is *already* non-functional at runtime — `getGanttConfig` already feeds it to `GanttConfigSchema.safeParse` and logs on failure. What moves is **when the author is told**, from console silence to an authoring-time refusal. That is `declared = enforced` restoration, not invented requiredness.

**Ablation stated before running, mutation proven on disk, restore proven by observation.** Prediction: reverting only the two production files while keeping the rewritten test fails exactly one assertion. Mutation confirmed by anchored `grep -c` counts (1→0 on both production lines, the old severed-state marker reappearing 0→1) rather than an editor exit code. Observed: `1 failed | 16 passed (17)`, the failure being precisely `expected [ Array(64) ] to include 'gantt'`. Restore confirmed by empty `git diff HEAD` plus `git hash-object` matching `HEAD:` for both files, inside a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`.

**The #6472 derived-pin family was reasoned about, not just re-run.** `FlatFaceGaps` is unmodified, and the dev gave the argument for why it cannot regress: adding `gantt` to `ObjectGanttSchema`'s declared keys grows only the `Exclude`'s *target* set, which cannot introduce residue on the source side. A green run plus a reason beats a green run.

## ⭐ The incidental find is the most valuable part, and it is now its own card

The dev's first draft of a docstring flipped an unrelated gate red. `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` scans **raw text** between `export const` boundaries for a `\bSpec[A-Z]\w*` token. The docstring sat above the private `GanttConfigExtensionFields` const — textually between the `ObjectTreeSchema` and `ObjectGanttSchema` boundaries — and mentioned `SpecGanttConfigSchema` **in prose**. The scanner charged that mention to `ObjectTreeSchema`, which references no spec schema at all.

So: **a comment changed a gate's verdict, and the red named an innocent neighbour.** Reworded here with a trap marker, which was the right call inside a gantt card's fence — but the gate is unchanged, so the next person writing a docstring in that file meets it with no warning. Filed as **#6705** with the three candidate directions (strip comments before scanning / parse instead of scan / fix the windowing independently of the token rule) and a warning that a naive fix could go green on the existing suite while destroying the gate.

**Scoring:** `minor`, correct — this narrows the accept set on a published schema, and objectui's own breaking changes ship as `minor` with the break spelled out.

**Fence held:** only the two production files, the one obsoleted pin, and the changeset. `packages/types/src/index.ts` and its `exports` map — held by #6527's B patch round — were not touched.
